description: All persistence is SQLite through the `api-core/storage` seam (no shared Postgres); Redis backs sessions, revocation, OAuth CSRF state, and rate limiting; schema changes are additive migrations, never recreation.

requirements.description: All durable state (users, credentials, sessions, refresh token families, realms, audit log, migrations) must be stored in SQLite accessed through the api-core/storage seam abstraction. No direct Postgres or other database dependencies are permitted. Redis is the exclusive store for hot state: session validity, revocation sets, OAuth CSRF nonces, and rate-limit counters. Schema changes must be delivered as additive migrations (add columns/tables only; no drop, rename, or recreation of existing structures).
requirements.title: SQLite Persistence via Storage Seam and Redis Hot State

validation.notes: api/internal/storage/sqlite_test.go: all CRUD operations go through the api-core/storage seam interface; no direct sql.DB calls outside the seam
api/internal/storage/migration_test.go: apply migrations in sequence on a blank SQLite file; assert schema version increments and no existing data is lost on re-run
api/internal/storage/migration_test.go: verify migrations are strictly additive — static analysis or schema diffing asserts no DROP TABLE, DROP COLUMN, or RENAME TABLE statements exist
api/handlers/auth/persistence_e2e_test.go: register a user, restart the service with the same SQLite file, sign in successfully — data survived restart
api/handlers/auth/persistence_e2e_test.go: revoke a session → revocation state appears in Redis within the same request cycle; new request with revoked token is rejected using Redis lookup
api/handlers/auth/persistence_e2e_test.go: OAuth CSRF nonce is written to Redis before redirect and consumed (deleted) after callback — replay of the same state param is rejected

title: SQLite Persistence via Storage Seam + Redis Hot State
